utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vujicic. That concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, who is the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, actually the next witness that we have scheduled is Mr. Pljevaljcic, and actually given the limited amount of time available, if the Chamber doesn't mind, I would actually prefer to start tomorrow morning with KW570, who has some time constraints. I want to make sure he finishes tomorrow, and then have Mr. Pljevaljcic testify after him. So if we could adjourn a little early today and have those two witnesses in that order tomorrow that would be the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When did that change of order of witnesses take place again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That hasn't taken place yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding was the next witness is KW570.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we had the two witnesses from Foca planned to be together, and then depending on the timing, we were expecting to have KW570 testify no later than first thing Friday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the Chamber hasn't been informed about this order between KW570 and Pljevaljcic. So could you pay attention to the notification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It looked like the Court was about to adjourn. That's the only reason I rose abruptly, Mr. President, if that's okay. And I simply did so because I wanted to address one point that the Court intended to defer. That's with respect to the admission of one of the two video-clips that were recently -- that were most recently played. And then the Court raised the question of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I don't think it's necessary to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It may not be. The reason I wanted to raise it, because it implicated matter of agreement that Mr. Robinson and I had in the earlier part of the case. The Court had asked a question, I don't know if it was a rhetorical question, about whether or not it would only go to credi -- it's not about the underlying ruling itself. It's about a question the Court asked about whether it would go to credibility. That implicates discussions that Mr. Robinson and I had much earlier in the case, objections that the Prosecution did not make to the admission of exhibits introduced by the Defence in the course of cross-examining Prosecution witnesses, and I thought that was appropriate to bring to the Court's attention because you may not have been aware of that and may not have remembered the whole course of the -- of the proceedings in that particular respect. So I'm not trying to revisit the -- the direct ruling on that issue, but I thought some indication about the history of the question the Court actually raised would be useful. And then I can tell the Court exactly why Mr. Robinson and I adopted that approach and why it's been used throughout the course of the entire case and why there has been -- why documents admitted when cross-examining a witness have been admitted for all purposes and not simply for credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber was about to issue an oral ruling on this matter, and that's why I told you that it was not necessary. In any event, I thank you for your submission, Mr. Tieger. It's about the Prosecution's request for the admission of the two video extracts bearing 65 ter 40199B, which depict an interview with Miroslav Stanic. The Chamber has considered the parties' submission on this matter as well as the witness's testimony in relation thereto. Keeping with its consistent practice that any third-party statements not prepared for the purposes of criminal proceedings may only be admitted -- excuse me. If they are commented upon, confirmed or adopted by the witness on the stand, the Chamber is of the view that the witness sufficiently commented on these two extracts for the purpose of admission. The Chamber shall therefore admit 65 ter 40199B into evidence. There are three more matters the Chamber wishes to deal with now. Shall we give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P6081. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The first matter is related to the 92 ter notification for Witness Desimir Sarenac, which was filed on the 20th of December, 2012. The Chamber observes that 189 of the 230 proposed associated exhibits have no English translation, and a further three are not on e-court. This makes it impossible to assess the admissibility of the proposed associated exhibits. The Chamber reminds the Defence that in the absence of English translation, the documents will not be admitted as associated exhibits. I would like to hear from you, Mr. Robinson, about whether the accused still intends to tender all 230 associated exhibits listed for this witness and why English translations have not been uploaded for 189 documents and why 3 of the documents are not uploaded on e-court at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's our intention to postpone the testimony of this witness because the translations were not able to be accomplished in time. This is actually the second time that we've had to postpone this testimony of this witness because of the large number of untranslated documents. But we've assessed that the documents are sufficiently important to us that we would like them to be admitted as associated exhibits, and so we will be trying to reschedule this witness's testimony. The language section promised us that they would have all these translations by the 23rd of January, with the caveat that if we didn't have other higher priorities, but we have since then had to make some documents higher priority for the witnesses for next week. So I don't know when we'll bring this witness, but at this point we do wish to persist in having those documents admitted, and we will do so -- bring the witness only when they're all translated and in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, the Chamber turns to the Prosecution's request for the admission of 65 ter 32786, an intercepted telephone conversation between Miroslav Gagovic and Fikret Abdic from the 15th of May, 1992, which admission was sought earlier today during the cross-examination of Janko Ivanovic. The Prosecution submits that this intercept is of the sort of intercepts Gagovic was shown and authenticated during his testimony. The accused's legal advisor responds that while the Defence is not concerned with the reliability of these intercepts in a vacuum, it wishes to ensure that the same standard are applied to the intercepts tendered by the Prosecution and the Defence. The Chamber recalls that its consistent practice, which was correctly applied by the Prosecution as recently as 15th of January, 2013, is that it is incumbent upon the party tendering an intercept to show you authenticity through a participant in the intercepted conversation, the relevant intercept operator, or the use of Rule 94(B) of the Tribunal's Rules. Given that this was not the case for 65 ter 32786, the Chamber is not satisfied of its authenticity. In addition, the Chamber notes that Ivanovic did not make a single comment on the intercept. On the contrary, he responded to the Prosecution's only question that he did not know. The Chamber will therefore not admit 65 ter 32786 into evidence. Finally, the Chamber will issue its decision on the accused's 75th motion for finding of disclosure violation filed on the 5th of December, 2012. The Chamber will also consider the Prosecution response filed on the 14th of December 2012. The 75th motion refers to a three and a half page statement of Witness KDZ485, which was disclosed to the accused in November 2012. The Chamber finds that the Prosecution violated Rule 66(A)(ii) by its failure to disclose the statement of Witness KDZ485 before the 7th of May, 2009, dead-line, for the disclosure of such material. The Prosecution has acknowledged this failure was due to human error. The Chamber reminds the Prosecution that such errors should have been identified and rectified well before the date of disclosure of the statement, which was disclosed three and a half years after the dead-line for disclosure of such material. However, having reviewed the content of the statement in light of KDZ485's evidence, the Chamber finds that its content is of limited or marginal relevance and not of such significance that the accused was prejudiced by this late disclosure. In the absence of prejudice, there's no basis to grant the accused's request that KDZ485 be recalled. Having said that, on my part I should refer to my partially dissenting opinion in the Chamber's decision on the accused's 37th to 42nd disclosure violation motions of 29th of March, 2011, and decline to make a finding of violation in the absence of prejudice to the accused. Unless there's anything to be raised, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 18th day of January, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.43 p.m.,
